extraction.name: CADS-dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale collection of 22,022 CT volumes with complete annotations for 167 anatomical structures from head to knees, consolidating data across 40 diverse public and hospital sources, designed for whole-body CT segmentation.
extraction.creator: Murong Xu, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Fernando Navarro, Maksym Fritsak, Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Suprosanna Shit, Bastian Wittmann, Sezgin Er, Sebastian M. Christ, Ezequiel de la Rosa, Julian Deseoe, Robert Graf, Hendrik Möller, Anjany Sekuboyina, Jan C. Peeken, Sven Becker, Giulia Baldini, Johannes Haubold, Felix Nensa, René Hosch, Nikhil Mirajkar, Saad Khalid, Stefan Zachow, Marc-André Weber, Georg Langs, Jakob Wasserthal, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, Andrey Fedorov, Ron Kikinis, Stephanie Tanadini-Lang, Jan S. Kirschke, Stephanie E. Combs, Bjoern Menze
extraction.rai:dataCollection: CT scans were aggregated from over 40 sources including public archives (e.g., TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K), medical imaging challenge collections (Grand Challenge, MICCAI, TCIA, Han-Seg, SAROS), and two newly contributed hospital datasets (484 anonymized head CTs and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CTs), spanning >100 imaging facilities across 16 countries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 4,695 (21%) of the initial 22,022 CT volumes contained partial annotations from public sources (often restricted to a single organ system), while approximately 79% contained no manual annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw CT scans sourced from 40 collections including TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K, VISCERAL, KiTS, LiTS, BTCV, CHAOS, VerSe, EXACT09, CAD-PE, RibFrac, Learn2reg, LNDb, LOLA11, SLIVER07, STOIC2021, EMPIRE10, AMOS, HaN-Seg, CT-ORG, LIDC-IDRI, CT Lymph Nodes, CPTAC, TCGA cohorts, RIDER Lung CT, Pancreas-CT, Istanbul Medipol University, and TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For patient privacy in newly acquired hospital head CT scans, a Gaussian filter (sigma = 5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) was applied to facial regions to obscure identity while preserving structural integrity near the face area.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were reoriented to standard RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) convention, resampled to uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and affine transformation matrices were simplified by removing rotation and translation components while preserving scaling and shear. For model input, intensities were scaled from 5th to 95th percentiles to [0, 1] with clipping.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were generated using a multi-stage automated pipeline: (1) Initial pseudo-labeling of all scans using specialized nnU-Net models trained on 9 anatomical groups using existing partial annotations; (2) Shape-informed quality control via auto-decoders based on implicit neural representations; (3) Multi-strategy label optimization comparing three model flavors (GT-flavor, Pseudo-flavor, Shape-flavor) using statistical ranking; (4) Hierarchical label assembly where GT labels overwrite pseudo-labels; complemented by manual annotations on VISCERAL Gold Corpus for 10 OARs by three medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist, and registration of Han-Seg CTs with the SimNIBS MRI atlas via ANTs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical tests (Shapiro-Wilk for normality, Levene's test for variance equality, followed by ANOVA, Welch's ANOVA, or Kruskal-Wallis with Tukey's HSD or Dunn's post-hoc tests at p < 0.05) evaluated Dice and HD95 metrics across flavors to determine the best model flavor per structure. A curation review of 65 TotalSegmentator test images by in-house medical professionals identified mislabeling, missing segments, and over-segmentation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: In-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist (JCP); external evaluation and test curation performed by clinical radiation oncologists and radiologists, including an experienced radiation oncologist with 5.5 years in practice.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net, ANTs, vesselFM, MIM software, auto-decoder with neural implicit functions
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Head CT scans from patients aged >= 18 years; facial features were intentionally blurred/anonymized using Gaussian filtering to protect patient identity.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to make comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers, advancing robust AI solutions in radiology and radiotherapy planning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Class imbalance across structures (e.g., upper cervical vertebrae C1-C5 and buccal mucosa occur less frequently than major organs). Known systematic omissions and boundary errors in baseline public ground-truth annotations (such as ribs and vertebrae in TotalSegmentator).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Exclusion of low-quality segmentations in shape-based QC may eliminate atypical pathological cases. Anatomical coverage ends at the knees (lacks hands and feet). Specific structures require refinement (brain mask includes all intracranial CNS tissue; optic chiasm is undersized; heart omits superior slices; rectum appears short; trachea includes air only without wall). Blurring of facial features prevents applications requiring detailed facial analysis.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Supervised training, testing, and validation of automated whole-body CT segmentation models; anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality image registration, tissue quantification for body composition analysis, radiation therapy planning, and population-level studies.
